title: Sadegh Hedayat's birth chart
metaDescription: Sadegh Hedayat's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.5° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Aquarius — the Sun, Mercury, Jupiter and Saturn. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Aquarius, but precisely: 27.5°, third decan, 20°–30°, under Venus in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 3.9° Aquarius, Venus was at 16.6° Pisces, Mars was at 16.3° Libra. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mercury and Saturn: 0.6° from an exact conjunction. The tradition stops reading a conjunction as two things. It is one appetite with two names, and it moves together or not at all. Behind it, Venus square Pluto at 1.1°, and Mars trine Pluto at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 27.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Pisces at 16.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Libra at 16.3° is in detriment; Saturn in Aquarius at 3.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 6 air, 2 water, 1 fire; by modality, 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 2 cardinal. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Libra into Scorpio during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.7° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
